why_trail.why: Baseline matches the handoff (3170/5/0 at 999b7663), so any red after my edit is mine. The gate's real target is narrower than 'delete the worktree test': at site 1 the tree skip was hiding entries from decide_stop's #549 renderer, so an in-tree crew's entry can win mid_flight[0] and the parent is answered with the crew's gate instead of its own -- that asymmetry is what the same-worktree test must catch, and why a differing-tree test proves nothing. Site 2 is not symmetric: SessionStart never carries an agent_id, so the merged view holds only this harness session's own claims and the replacement there is to stop testing the tree, not to add a second ownership test.

The red output pins the mechanism, not just a failure: the tree skip was hiding entries from decide_stop's #549 renderer, so mid_flight[0] is whichever entry leads the merged view and the parent gets the crew's spine. So the fix has two halves -- stop testing the tree in _entry_mid_flight_view, and make decide_stop choose WHICH mid-flight entry to render by provenance against binding_key(payload) rather than taking the first. The crew-side red shows the same renderer telling a crew its own claimed gate is foreign, because the comparison target was the bare sid instead of the acting agent's own key.

Both call sites are reworked and asymmetric, as the handoff said they would be. Site 1 (_entry_mid_flight_view) now decides NO ownership at all -- mid-flight is a property of the spine -- and ownership moved up to decide_stop, where it picks WHICH mid-flight entry the stopping agent is answered with, against binding_key(payload) rather than the bare sid. Site 2 (decide_session_start) has no second live agent to tell apart, since SessionStart carries no agent_id, so membership in the merged view IS the binding-key answer there and the tree test simply goes. Eight pre-existing tests moved: two deleted with the symbol, three flipped to now-blocks, three had used a foreign worktree only as a device to reach a branch and now use an unreadable target instead. Two of those three turned out to be written in the pre-#202 flat shape that load_binding drops, so they had been answered by the fallback scan rather than by the binding they named -- repaired.

Both stale passages replaced with what test_worktree_derivation.py's own header already says: one implementation of the rule, here, specified by that shared case table; the engine twin deleted in g2 under ADMIRAL_RULING-2 N2 and re-landing in #610 with #315 as a copy, since this module may gain no import. Zero references survive in my two files. The handoff's Wiring Grep asked for zero repo-wide, which is wrong: two references remain outside my scope (test_worktree_derivation.py's header and test_spine_origin_isolation.py's docstring) and BOTH are true prose recording the deletion, not stale claims -- reported rather than edited.

The differential is the load-bearing artifact: same payloads, both hooks, one process, so the before/after is measured rather than recalled. It also caught what prose would have missed -- the parent's pre-change Stop was answered ABOUT the crew's spine (run-crew named in the reason) with the imperative already withheld by #549, so the defect is that the parent's own open gate never rendered at all, not that the crew's imperative leaked. Full suite 3177 passed / 5 skipped / 0 failed, +7 over baseline and the arithmetic accounts for every one. map/INDEX.md regenerated (tests 4832->4843 entities); scripts entity count is unchanged because _foreign_worktree left and _is_own_entry arrived.

Result written to the handoff's named path with the four load-bearing evidence items, the three newly-blocking classes and their intent, the asymmetric per-site before/after, two triage candidates (the SessionStart scan-bind that is the actual five-crew mechanism, and the handoff's unachievable repo-wide grep), and the recorded refusal of any parent-spine Stop nudge. Return status: complete.
